title: Sparklines Lexicon + Alert Variance Notes
summary: Working notes: define a compact lexicon for sparkline patterns, map each pattern to investigation hypotheses and sampling/trace anchors; propose alert variance handling for low-volume metrics; dashboard micro-panel recommendations to reduce query cost and improve operator signal-to-noise.
body:
Problem statement:
Many of our inference dashboards rely on small sparkline widgets and single-number alerts for throughput/latency/kv-warmth signals. Operators report too many noisy alerts for low-volume tenants and panels that hide transient but important patterns. This doc proposes: 1) a concise lexicon for sparkline patterns so that panels and runbooks speak the same language; 2) guidance to set variance-aware alerts for sparse metrics; 3) trace/span annotation anchors to attach when a pattern is observed; 4) panel design notes that balance visibility and query cost.

1) Sparkline pattern lexicon (compact, for panel titles and runbooks)
- flatline: near-zero variance for window (median ~0). Hypothesis: service disconnected / probe stopped / metric instrumenting failure.
- noise-jitter: median stable, short high-frequency noise (spikes 1-3x). Hypothesis: transient load sources or contended CPU on host; check service-level CPU and batch-size distribution.
- sustained-step-up: sudden sustained increase >50% baseline for >window. Hypothesis: traffic shift, rollout of a higher-throughput model variant, or upstream fanout.
- decay-slope: gradual decline over hours. Hypothesis: cache eviction, slow burn of token-level failures, or tenant throttling.
- ping-pong: alternating spikes and troughs (periodic). Hypothesis: autoscale or probe alignment issue.
- clipped-ceiling: flat near a maximum (saturation). Hypothesis: capacity limit hit (gpu queue full / batching cap).
- long-tail-tails: heavy right skew in sample distribution (high quantiles >> median). Hypothesis: variable input sizes or cascade fallback to slow model.
- burstburst: infrequent but large amplitude bursts. Hypothesis: cron jobs, batch replays, or import jobs.

Usage: prefix panel titles with [spark:pattern] e.g., "[spark:decay-slope] inference.requests/s (tenant X)". Include canonical investigator hint inline in panel tooltip (one-liner).

2) Alert variance policy (for low-volume and multi-tenant signals)
Goals: reduce noise, keep sensitivity to real regressions, keep costs bounded.
Rules:
- Use variance-aware thresholds: combine absolute and relative thresholds. Example: alert when (p95 > baseline * 1.5 AND absolute delta > X) OR (absolute delta > Y). Set X proportional to median volume and Y as a hard floor.
- Min-sample gating: do not evaluate percentile alerts if sample_count < min_samples (e.g., 30 samples in window). For telemetry that naturally has fewer samples (low-traffic tenants), prefer session-level traces or synthetic probes.
- Window-adaptive thresholds: for bursty signals use shorter windows for detection (5m) but require confirmation in a longer window (30m) before firing page-level alerts.
- Severity tiers: noisy deviations create slack-level (incidents-notified-to-channel) alerts, sustained confirmed deviations create page-level alerts.
- Alert bucketing: group noisy alerts by tenant shard + model_variant + region to limit alert cardinality.

Example rule (text):
- Metric: inference.response.time_ms.p95
- Baseline: 95th percentile computed rolling 7d per model_variant
- Fire condition: (current_p95 > baseline * 1.6 AND sample_count >= 50) OR (current_p95 - baseline_abs > 200ms AND sample_count >= 20)
- Confirm: condition holds in 2/3 consecutive evaluation windows (5m each) -> escalate to page.

3) Trace and span anchors to attach when patterns observed
To make triage faster, when panels show certain patterns the operator should capture lightweight trace anchors. Attachments should be small JSON blobs or links to existing trace ids. Proposed span annotations to add at instrument time: 
- span.tag:service.layer = inference-serving
- span.tag:model.variant = <model_variant>
- span.tag:tenant.hash = <sha1-tenant> (pseudonymized)
- span.tag:batch.size = <int>
- span.tag:kvcache.hit = true|false
- span.tag:prefix.cache.warmth = <0-1>
- span.tag:response.type = streaming|nonstreaming
- span.event:request.size_tokens = <int> (only top-level span)
- span.event:route = <api-route>
Why: these tags let us quickly pivot traces for hypotheses in the lexicon: e.g., if decay-slope + kvcache.hit=false -> investigate eviction metrics and prefetch scheduling.

Sampling guidance for anchors:
- If pattern == flatline -> capture sampler of last 10 associated traces and verify instrumentation heartbeat.
- If pattern == long-tail-tails -> tail-sample at p99/p999 using our existing tail-sampler job; attach one full trace and 3 lightweight spans.
- If sustained-step-up -> increase trace sampling for affected model_variant to 10% for 30m. Record sampling-rate change in metadata.

4) Dashboard micro-panel and cost notes
Design goals: show patterns at-a-glance, minimize expensive queries, and allow fast jump-to-trace.
Panel patterns: 
- Micro-sparklines: single-series, 30–90px height, pre-aggregated to 1m resolution. Use materialized rollup tables for heavy metrics.
- Small-multiples: use sparkline small-multiples for top N tenants (N=12 max) to avoid cardinality explosion. Provide a selector to switch to all-tenant heatmap only when needed.
- Composite single-number: show current value, delta vs baseline, and tiny sparkline inline to reduce panel count.
- Distribution thumbnail: show median and p95/p999 whiskers compactly for latency signals (one SQL-style query that returns quartiles).

Query optimizations:
- Prefer precomputed rollups for 1m/5m windows instead of raw-timeseries.
- Use query-time sample gating to avoid heavy percentile computations on low-sample windows.
- Cache panel queries for 30s to 60s when acceptable.

Cost control
- Tag dashboards as "query-cost-aware"; dashboards with >50 dependent queries require owner justification.
- Provide a cost estimate header: rough token/compute estimate per refresh for the dashboard (text field).

5) Runbook snippets (operator-first)
- If sparkline shows [flatline]: check last exporter heartbeat (exporter.heartbeats) -> if missing, reload exporter process; if present, escalate instrumentation owner.
- If [long-tail-tails] on latency: run tail-sampler for affected model_variant; look for changed input_length distribution; check fallback logs (model-selection).
- If [clipped-ceiling] on concurrency: check GPU queue depth, batching cap, model_variant parallelism setting; consider quick fallback to smaller model_variant for critical tenants.

6) Metric entropy reduction checklist (practical steps)
- Rename ad-hoc metrics to canonical names (example mapping list below).
- Add provenance tags to metrics at emit-time: origin=svc, pipeline=ingest, schema_version=1.
- Enforce tenant bucketing policy: only emit per-tenant time series for top-k tenants; else emit sampled tenant_histograms.
- Replace per-tenant percentile queries with sketch-based approximations or aggregated histograms where possible.
- Deprecate duplicate metrics: keep a deprecation log and 30d forwarding window.

Canonical metric name proposals (short list):
- inference.request.count
- inference.request.size_tokens.p50,p95
- inference.response.first_byte_ms.p50,p95,p999
- inference.response.total_ms.p50,p95,p999
- inference.kvcache.hit_rate (0-1)
- inference.batch.size.mean
- inference.failed.requests.count
- telemetry.exporter.heartbeat_seconds_since

7) Action items and owners (short-term)
- [Asha] draft dashboard template with title-prefix usage and tooltips -> JIRA-OBS-2147 (in progress)
- [Marco] add span tags model.variant + batch.size to python-serving SDK -> PR:433 (review)
- [Priya] implement min-sample gating helper lib used by alert rules -> JIRA-OBS-2178 (todo)
- [Evan] build a lightweight rollup for inference.response.total_ms 1m resolution -> JIRA-OBS-2199 (in progress)

Open questions / discussion points:
- Minimum sample thresholds: should they be absolute or relative to tenant historical volume? (suggest hybrid).
- How aggressive do we want automated sampling-rate changes on step-up detections? (safety + cost tradeoffs).
- Should we auto-instrument exporter heartbeats into dashboards as a separate small panel? (favored).

Appendix: short SQL examples (illustrative)
- Precomputed p95 rollup ingestion: INSERT INTO rollups.inference_latency_1m (ts, model_variant, p95) SELECT window_start, model_variant, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) FROM raw.inference_latency GROUP BY window_start, model_variant;
- Min-sample gating example for alert: SELECT count(*) as samples, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) FROM rollups.inference_latency_1m WHERE ts > now() - interval '5 minutes' AND model_variant = 'rwd-1b'; then gate on samples >= 50 before evaluating percentile thresholds.

End notes: this is intentionally compact. If we adopt the lexicon and alert-variance rules we should be able to reduce noisy paging by ~30–50% on pilot dashboards and increase time-to-first-diagnosis for true regressions. Feedback requested from oncall rotation and instrumentation owners (Marco, Priya).
